newsitem.title: CHINA: U.S. congressman wary on Taiwan plane delivery.
newsitem.headline: U.S. congressman wary on Taiwan plane delivery.

text.p: U.S. congressman John LaFalce said on Friday he was concerned about how China would react to the delivery of F-16 fighter aircraft to Taiwan, expected to begin in about a year.
LaFalce, one of a delegation of 22 U.S. congressional representatives visiting China, told reporters that Taiwan remained the most sensitive issue between China and the United States.
"One concern of mine is the obligation of the United States on the basis of legislation passed in 1979 to provide Taiwan with adequate defence," the New York Democrat said.
He said delivery of the 150 F-16 fighters to replace ageing F-5s, agreed by President George Bush in 1992, would begin in about a year's time.
"It is my hope that the Chinese people will understand that the law has to be honoured," he said.

The United States shifted diplomatic recognition from Taipei to Beijing in 1979, but at the same time Congress passed into law legislation requiring the United States to continue to provide defence for the island province.
LaFalce, who last visited China in 1979, said he was stunned by the changes in the country, and said China and the United States now had far more in common than they did before.
"The U.S.-China relationship is the most important bilateral relationship for at least the next 50 years, not only for the U.S., but also for the world," he said.
